_meta.title: Blaze Camp equipment usage and training-variable grammar (reference tabs)

conventions.OBSERVED: read from a cell (tab + cell given)
conventions.SCIENCE: general exercise-science background, not the coach's words
conventions.CHAT: the coach's words in the workflow brief (not in a sheet)

_meta.parser_note: Tags in exercise_parses come from a keyword lexicon (scratchpad/refvars_eq_agent/extract.py). implement_source = explicit (word in the cell) / default_inferred (e.g. 'Lat pull downs' -> cable, 'Pushups' -> bodyweight) / unresolved. Treat default_inferred as INFERRED.

grammar.formula: EXERCISE = PATTERN x IMPLEMENT x EXTERNAL_STABILITY x LOAD_POSITION x LOAD_LATERALITY x STANCE/BASE x GRIP x FEET/BODY_POSITION x ROM x END_RANGE x ACCOMMODATING_RESISTANCE x PLANE_PERTURBATION ; DOSE = LOAD_MAGNITUDE x SPEED/INTENT x VOLUME ; ATHLETIC = FORCE_PHASE x SPEED/INTENT x IMPLEMENT

variables.name: PATTERN (base movement)
variables.owner_note: Owned by the taxonomy team; listed here only so the grammar is complete.

coach_labels.verbatim: codes AP (athletic patterns), CT/CP (control/core), RP (resistance patterns), BS (bilateral), UL (unilateral)

variables.equipment_relevance: Pattern decides WHICH implements can carry it (e.g. a vertical pull needs a bar, cable, band or TRX anchor; a knee-dominant pattern can be loaded by anything from bodyweight to barbell). See equipment_coverage.

variables.name: IMPLEMENT (what provides the resistance)

coach_labels.verbatim: ***This model is based on free weight squats, leg presses and machines will be covered at the end... Scroll bellow the squats

coach_chat_statements: Machines have a lot of reference points / constraints ... you can push a lot, and it's safer.
Free weights are very different. Barbells are more skilled. Dumbbells, kettlebells, medicine balls...
If you read the workouts you can understand them by their equipment usage.
variables.values_observed: see implements[] (counts per implement across 701 exercise cells)
what_it_changes_per_coach: Machine = high constraint, high push, low stabilisation demand, safer; preferred for volume, injured and older clients (chat).
Barbell = most skilled free weight (chat); heavy barbell = slow eccentric = more recruitment, light barbell = fast eccentric = less recruitment (SQ A44:A48).
Split grips (DB/KB) instead of fixed grips (barbell/bars) when joints hurt (program banners, see cross_check).
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: guided machines reduce the degrees of freedom the lifter must stabilise, so a larger share of effort goes to the target muscle and technical failure is less likely (better stimulus-to-fatigue ratio for hypertrophy; Israetel). Free weights add stabiliser demand and transfer better to unconstrained sport movement but cost more skill and systemic fatigue. Neither builds more muscle per hard set when sets are taken close to failure.
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: implement is chosen AFTER pattern, from what the client owns, then biased by client profile: volume-seeking / injured / older -> machine or supported variant first; athlete -> free weight + ballistic implements; joint pain -> DB/KB (split grip) or unilateral.

variables.name: EXTERNAL STABILITY / REFERENCE POINTS (how much the equipment holds you)

coach_labels.verbatim: Foam roller or swiss ball wall assisted goblet
Incline DB bench press feet on wall

coach_chat_statements: You sit down, put your feet on the ground, and move your hands or your feet. Those have a lot of constraints. You can push a lot, but it's also safer.
For people who want to go up in volume, people who have injuries, or people who are older, more machines are usually better for being able to push without having to worry about stabilization.

values.value: cable (fixed line of pull, free body)
supported free weight (seat / bench / chest pad / floor / wall / box)
examples: Foam roller or swiss ball wall assisted goblet (RP A12, green)

values.value: unsupported free weight, reduced base (tall kneeling, half kneeling, Z-floor)
examples: DB Z press on floor (RP E10, yellow)

values.value: no base / airborne (feet in air, overhead, ballistic)
examples: feet in air (hollow legs str8) (RP I28, red)

variables.what_it_changes_per_coach: More reference points -> more load you can push safely and less skill needed (chat). The vertical-push column is coloured green (seated) -> yellow (Z floor, tall kneeling DB) -> red (kneeling barbell, standing): difficulty rises as the support is removed (OBSERVED RP E8:E15).
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: force output in a lift is limited by the weakest link in the chain; external support removes trunk/hip stabilisation as the limiter, so the prime mover can be loaded closer to its own capacity (e.g. seated vs standing press, chest-supported vs bent-over row).
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: map client flags {older, injured, deconditioned, hypertrophy-volume} -> prefer rank 1-3; {athlete, advanced, sport transfer} -> allow rank 4-6 in the first strength slot, keep rank 1-3 for accessory volume.

variables.name: LOAD POSITION (where the weight sits on the body)

coach_labels.verbatim: *The squat is considered a KNEE DOMINANT movement, therefore how we load the weight of the squat can play a big role in how effective it may be
**The easiest way for me to define a loading principle is by going from most front loaded to most back loaded, so just try it and let me know
**THIS EASY TO HARD MODEL IS TO DETERMINE HOW HARD OR EASY IS TO DO THE SQUAT WITH MAXIMAL UPRIGHT POSTURE & HIPS GOIN DOWN

values.position: at the sides (suitcase, centre of mass over mid-foot)
front, chest height, held in hands
front, high in the elbow crease

medball_positions.verbatim: Medball down over front leg FFE

variables.what_it_changes_per_coach: Front -> back loading changes how hard it is to stay upright with the hips going down (SQ A9); load position moves the demand UP/DOWN and SIDE2SIDE (LU A18). The HIGH list in RP C31 is the same front->back->overhead order as the squat ladder, so one ladder serves bilateral and unilateral knee-dominant work.
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: the system centre of mass must stay over mid-foot. A load in front acts as a counterweight that allows an upright torso and deeper knee flexion (bigger knee-extensor moment = 'knee dominant'); moving the load back forces trunk inclination and shifts moment to the hip extensors; overhead adds thoracic, shoulder and ankle mobility demands. Higher loads (shoulder, zercher, rack) lengthen the lever on the trunk vs low suitcase loads.
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: rank 1-2 for beginners or poor upright posture; rank 1-5 for quad/knee-dominant goals; rank 6-7 for heavier/fewer-rep strength; rank 8 only with the overhead/snatch progression (OL). If the client lacks the implement, move to the nearest rank whose implement they own (hex->goblet DB/KB; front squat->double KB front rack (RP A18) or high zercher DB (RP A19)).
equipment_substitution_ladder: Double front rack kb squat (RP A18)

GET OUT OF THE HIP - MODERATE

values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: symmetric load, no extra frontal/transverse moment at the stance hip.

values.coach_effect: GET INTO THE HIP (RP C19/C23/C71); 'Split stance ALWAYS contralateral' (RP G83)
values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: load opposite the stance leg increases the adduction / internal-rotation moment on the stance hip; the hip must accept the pelvis 'into' it and push out of it (gait-like, opposite arm/leg).

values.coach_effect: GET OUT OF THE HIP (RP C21/C25/C73)
values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: load over the stance side biases the hip out (abduction/external rotation) and moves demand to the opposite-side trunk (QL, obliques).

verbatim_examples: One up/one down Alternating DB floor press (RP I30)
One forward/one back Alternating cable press (RP I31)
values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: two implements out of phase create a rotational demand on the trunk.

verbatim_examples: kneeling pushups one hand higher (RP I32)
values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: asymmetric hand height loads one side more without a second implement.
INFERRED: unilateral limb, anti-rotation demand on trunk.

variables.difficulty_rule: OBSERVED: suitcase-height contra/ipsi = 'MODERATE' (RP C19/C21); front-racked contra/ipsi = 'HARDER' (RP C23/C25). Higher load position = harder.
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: an off-centre load creates an external frontal-plane moment about the stance hip equal to load x horizontal distance; hip abductors (glute med/min) and trunk lateral flexors must produce the opposing moment. Contralateral loading (hand opposite stance leg) has been shown to raise gluteus medius activity in split squats/step-ups relative to ipsilateral.
variables.equipment_relevance: Requires a SINGLE implement or two unequal ones (one DB, one KB, one medball). A client with only one dumbbell can still run the whole INTO/OUT-of-hip family.
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: athletes / frontal-transverse goals -> contralateral first (MODERATE), ipsilateral second; progress suitcase -> on shoulder -> high zercher -> front racked.

variables.name: STANCE / BASE OF SUPPORT

coach_labels.verbatim: Stance loads the FRONT TO BACK
**Just because they are knee dominant, it doesn't mean that they don't affect the hips... We can bias different foot placement for hip adaptations as much as foot adaptations

values: Front and Rear foot elevated lunge
Half kneeling same side leg up
Half kneeling opposite side leg up

values.group: base ladder for pressing (RP E8:E15, colour)

values: half kneeling facing L/R with LEFT LEG UP / RIGHT LEG FORWARD (BA C65:C68)

variables.what_it_changes_per_coach: Stance loads FRONT TO BACK (LU A17); foot placement biases hip vs foot adaptations (LU A4); lunges are 'a propulsive strategy' (LU A8) and 'great for finding/gaining/regaining ROM' (LU A12).
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: front-foot elevation increases front hip/knee flexion range (more stretch on glute max/adductors); rear-foot elevation shifts most of the bodyweight onto the front leg; reverse lunges and step-ups are concentric-propulsive, forward lunges add a deceleration (eccentric braking) component.
variables.equipment_relevance: Most stance variables need only a bench/box/plate (household objects). FFE needs a plate or step; RFE needs a bench; 'rear foot against wall' needs a wall.
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: bilateral -> staggered -> split (floor) -> FFE/RFE -> FFE+RFE -> single leg; half kneeling variants for rows/presses when anti-rotation is the goal.

variables.name: HAND PLACEMENT / GRIP
values_in_names: Shoulder width grip / Wide grip / Snatch grip barbell deadlift (RP A71:A73)
palms forward / Palms down / spill the can (RP K8:K10)
variables.joint_pain_rule: OBSERVED in program banners (cross-check, not a reference tab): '****When there are joint pains, usually getting away from fixed grips (barbells, bars) and going split grips (dumbbells, kbs, indivitual grips) help take care of some stuff' (EXAMPLE UPPERLOWER SPLIT A7, PUSHPULLLEGS A7); ATHLETIC FULL BODY A6 adds 'usually going unilateral or/and also'.
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: a fixed bar locks wrist/forearm rotation and shoulder path; dumbbells/KBs let the joints self-select a path, which commonly reduces elbow/shoulder discomfort. Grip width changes ROM (snatch grip deadlift = longer pull) and shoulder angle (wide vs close pulldown).
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: grip is the cheapest variety lever inside a block (same implement, new stimulus angle). Joint-pain flag -> replace bar with DB/KB or cable handles.

variables.name: END-RANGE BEHAVIOUR (what happens at the bottom)

coach_labels.verbatim: **PULSING/REP BOUNCING IS FOR TRANSITIONAL OR AMMORTIZATION PHASE

values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: implement comes to rest; each rep starts concentric-only (no stretch-shortening help); resets technique.
INFERRED: brief contact then rebound; uses elastic return; continuous tension.
INFERRED: never touches; eccentric-first, turnaround at hamstring end range.
INFERRED: sit and release on the box (posterior-chain reset, dead-stop-like), opposite of 'touch & go' on the box.
INFERRED: dead stop on safety pins.
landing absorbed to a stop (TAKING IN FORCES).

values.coach_effect: **PULSING/REP BOUNCING IS FOR TRANSITIONAL OR AMMORTIZATION PHASE (BA C21)
PLYOMETRIC PURPOSE - BE REACTIVE & BOUNCY (BA D22)

values.value: Receive pause/creat -> Receive/create -> Repeat receive create
values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: the plyo version of dead stop -> touch & go -> continuous rebound, graded by zone.

variables.science_note: SCIENCE: a pause of >~1-2 s at the bottom dissipates most stored elastic energy and potentiation, making the concentric harder and more 'pure' (useful for strength off the bottom and technique); touch-and-go exploits the stretch-shortening cycle; an RDL-style turnaround trains eccentric control at long muscle length.
variables.equipment_relevance: Dead stop needs a floor/pins/box; box variants need a box; the rest are technique instructions (no equipment).
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED: beginners dead stop, intermediates touch & go, advanced RDL / repeat. Plyo zone 1 -> 2 -> 3 mirrors the same order.

values.load: Weight should be lower ranges and fast speed (SQ B38)
values.coach_detail: Helps you have a faster concentric reaction & increase velocity of your against gravity forces (SQ C37)
values.who: SOMEBODY THAT IS SLOW ON THE WAY UP (SQ D38)

values.mechanical_effect: INFERRED: bands anchored overhead unload the bottom (assistance) and fade toward the top -> faster exit from the hole; on jumps = assisted overspeed.

BILATERAL DROP WEIGHTED, DELOAD WEIGHT & JUMP (BA C40)
UNILATERAL DROP WEIGHTED, DELOAD WEIGHT & HOP/JUMP (BA C42/C44)
DB Depth drop dbs Jump (S23 I12)
values.mechanical_effect: SCIENCE: accentuated eccentric loading - extra load on the way down only, released at the bottom, lighter concentric.

variables.coach_summary: Bands = speed/velocity, around 50%; chains = magnitude/loading/stiffness, around 70% (SQ C35, C39, B36, B40).
variables.science_note: SCIENCE: accommodating resistance matches the ascending strength curve of squats/presses/deadlifts; bands (elastic, tension rises with stretch) add eccentric speed and reduce lockout deceleration; chains add mass progressively; meta-analyses show small benefits for strength/power vs constant load when used at moderate loads with fast intent. Weight releasers = accentuated eccentric loading (supramaximal eccentric, potentiated concentric).
variables.equipment_relevance: Bands are the cheapest power tool in the whole system: the only accommodating option that works at home (band + jump = reverse-banded hops). Chains and weight releasers are gym-only.
variables.generator_rule: INFERRED from SQ D36/D38/D40: diagnosis -> tool. Can't descend well -> bottom bands; slow out of the bottom -> reverse bands; soft/collapses -> chains. All marked ADVANCED (RP red / BYOP ADVANCED); only for intermediate+ clients with an athletic/strength goal.

'FAST RPE6 or about 60-70%' (4 TRACKS N17, N21)

statements.verbatim: *The squat is considered a KNEE DOMINANT movement, therefore how we load the weight of the squat can play a big role in how effective it may be
**The easiest way for me to define a loading principle is by going from most front loaded to most back loaded, so just try it and let me know
***This model is based on free weight squats, leg presses and machines will be covered at the end... Scroll bellow the squats
statements.interpretation_INFERRED: Free weights are the base model; machines are an appendix, i.e. the coach thinks in free weights first and adds machines as a separate category.

statements.verbatim: ****Modify sets/reps as you want, just don't go too far into changing it, you may ruin the stimulus
*****Follow the RIR prescription - REPS IN RESERVE - You will also see RPE
**THIS EASY TO HARD MODEL IS TO DETERMINE HOW HARD OR EASY IS TO DO THE SQUAT WITH MAXIMAL UPRIGHT POSTURE & HIPS GOIN DOWN

**MYO SET is where you do 15 reps, without stopping you just dont move for 3 seconds (resting) then do another 5 reps, breathe/rest 3 seconds, and repeat for 5 sets of those 5 reps... Totalis 40 reps without a stop. You can youtube myoreps and see more info about them.
statements.interpretation_INFERRED: Myo set; 3-second rests; local fatigue -> machine/isolation-friendly.
Heavy barbell is paired with slow eccentric and MORE recruitment.
Light barbell is paired with fast eccentric and LESS recruitment; this is the sheet version of the chat's 'heavier = slower, lighter = faster'.

open_questions: Weight releasers: SQ B41:D41 say 'I HAVE NO IDEA'. Should the generator leave them out, or use them as accentuated-eccentric tools for advanced strength athletes (same physics as BA C38:C44 'DROP WEIGHTED, DELOAD WEIGHT')?

Medball loads: the sheets never give a weight. Is 8-10 lb the default for ALL throws (chest pass, overhead, scoops), and what weight for slams (C60, C76:C81) and 'CORE EXTRAS' (C83:C89)? Different for youth/women/older clients?

'*RDL' is the red last value in ROM VARIABLE, END RANGE BEHAVIOR VARIABLE and LOADING VARIABLES (RP A85, A89, A94). What does it mean in each list: an RDL-style turnaround, a top-down start, or a placeholder?

ROM 'Elevated' (RP A82, green): block/rack pulls (shorter ROM) or elevated feet (longer ROM, like 'Elevated feet on bench glute bridge' A62 and 'Elevated Push ups (for full ROM)' S23 Z11)? The two meanings change ROM in opposite directions.
Low bar is 'HARDEST' in SQ G10 but yellow (intermediate) in RP A24. Is the squat ladder a posture-difficulty rank only, separate from the client level?

Machines: only 4 have an opinion (LEG PRESS / PENDULUM 'LOVE IT', HACK SQUAT 'I PERSONALLY DON'T LIKE IT', V-SQUAT never). What are your opinions on Smith machine squats (used in EXAMPLE FAT BURN G8), hip thrust machine, leg curl, GHD, reverse hyper, belt squat?

For older / injured / volume clients (chat: 'more machines are usually better'): is there a minimum share of machine work, or a list of free-weight lifts they should never get (e.g. overhead squat, snatch, low bar)?

Equipment profiles: which home set-ups do clients actually report (bodyweight only, DBs only, KB only, bands only, garage barbell)? Should a bands-only client get banded versions of every pattern, or bodyweight + bands only for pulls/power?
Joint-pain banner says swap fixed grips for split grips (DB/KB). Does that also cover machines with neutral handles, and cables?

Horizontal-before-vertical (chat) is not written in any reference tab, and the library lists vertical first. Is the rule 'every session' or 'only when both appear in the same session'? Does it also hold for unilateral work and for athletes?
'Whats that strap rotating in/out' (RP A54:A55): which product is it (e.g. a hip-rotation band/strap)? We need the name for an equipment checklist.
'Kong Rows' (RP G77): which implement/set-up is this?
Bands '~50%' and chains '~70%': % of what (bar weight at the bottom, or 1RM of the lift without bands)? How much band/chain tension (e.g. light/average/strong band)?
'Box *ANY Squat' (RP A25:A30): can ANY loading from the 8-rank ladder go on the box, including overhead (OL A25 'OVERHEAD BOX SQUAT')?
French contrast I18 has 4 exercises but reps '3/3/3/3/3' (5 slots) and sets '3-4' (auto-dated G18). Which exercise takes the 5th slot, and should 'Goblet squats' be goblet squat JUMPS?
Hop vs jump: in BA every phase lists both HOP and JUMP. Is HOP = small-amplitude ankle-stiffness contact and JUMP = full triple extension?
Plyo zones (S23 C34:D36 'Receive pause/creat', 'Receive/create', 'Repeat receive create'): is this the same ladder as Dead stop -> Touch & go -> continuous rebound in the resistance tab?
Aerobic sheet is running only. For clients who cannot run (older, injured), should the A/B/C colour work transfer to bike/rower/ski erg with the same work:rest, and which erg do you prefer?
